Section 173(1) Of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Praying To Set
Aside The Judgment And Award Dated 12.07.2011 In Mvc
No.804/2009 Passed By The Fast Track Court-Iii And
Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi, By
Allowing This Appeal With Cost And Etc.,.

This Appeal Coming On For Final Hearing This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award in MVC No.804/2009, dated 12.07.2011 passed by the Fast Track Court-III and Additional MACT, Belagavi,
questioning the liability fastened on it to pay compensation, on the ground that the deceased has travelled in the pick-up van as a gratuitous passenger but not as owner of load of jaggery.

sentences.text: 2 2. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
3. In this case, the factum of accident, death of deceased in the said accident are not in dispute.
The only disputed fact is that whether the deceased was a gratuitous passenger or travelled along with goods of jaggery.
4. The learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that there is no evidence that the deceased was travelling in pick-up van along with load of jaggary.
Therefore, submitted that the deceased was travelling as a gratuitous passenger.
Hence, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the deceased was travelling along with load of jaggery in the pick-up van and it is deposed by the claimant No.1 who is wife of deceased and also by the driver of the pick-up van that the deceased was a traveller in the pick-up van as owner of load of NC: 2023:KHC-D:13267 jaggery.
Therefore, justified the judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
6. The factum of accident and death of deceased is not disputed.
Whether the deceased has travelled in the goods vehicle as a gratuitous passenger or as owner of the load of jaggery is to be considered.
7. Ex.P.1 is the complaint which is in Marathi language and appended with Kannada translation.
The said complaint is given by the Police Constable.
Upon going through the factum of accident, in the said complaint it is reported that goods tempo was turtled and there was a load of jaggery in the goods tempo.
It is true that the claimants have not produced any document for having purchased jaggery by the deceased.
It is proved that except the driver and the deceased, there were no other persons travelling in the goods tempo along with goods.

The driver of goods tempo is examined as RW.2 and in his evidence he has stated that the deceased had NC: 2023:KHC-D:13267 purchased jaggery at Harugeri and was taking the jaggery to market at Miraj and Sangli for selling the same.
8.
The evidence in this regard is to be considered on all its preponderance of probabilities.
The goods tempo was loaded with jaggery.
Except the deceased, there were no other persons travelling in the goods tempo in the cabin.
Therefore, there were only two persons namely the driver who was driving the goods tempo and the deceased was sitting beside the driver.
The claimant has stated that her husband the deceased has taken load of jaggery in the goods tempo to sell the same in the markets of Sangli and Miraj.

9. Just because there is no evidence that the claimant has claimed jaggery or not from the place of accident or from the police station is not a ground to suspect the evidence of claimant and RW.2 regarding the goods tempo was loaded with jaggery.
The deceased died and the claimants might have left jaggery there itself.

Therefore just because the claimant has not claimed NC:
2023:KHC-D:13267 jaggery is not a ground to suspect the evidence that the deceased has travelled in the goods tempo along with load of jaggery.

sentences.text: In this regard the tribunal has correctly assessed and analyzed the evidence on record.
In the goods tempo the load of jaggery was also not a small quantity but it is 300 blocks of each weighing 10 kgs.
Therefore, considering all these evidences on all its preponderance of probabilities, it is proved that the deceased has travelled in the goods tempo along with load of jaggery.
Hence in this regard there is no good ground to cause interference with the finding given by the tribunal.
Therefore the liability fastened on the insurance company to pay compensation is liable to be confirmed.
11. The tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 8% p.a.
The same is scaled down to 6% p.a.
Therefore, so far as rate of interest is concerned, the appeal filed by the insurance company is liable to be allowed in part.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award in MVC No.804/2009, dated 12.07.2011, passed by the Fast Track Court-III and Addl. MACT, Belagavi, stands modified.
iii) The liability fastened on the insurance company to pay compensation is confirmed.
iv) The claimant is entitled for compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till realization.
 v) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
vi) No order as to costs.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13267  vii) Draw award accordingly.

SD/-
